title: Predictive prefetch and reservation: model-specific memory profile tuning for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Long-context variants for Llama/Mistral/Qwen show intermittent OOMs and tail-latency spikes when continuous batching collides with KV residency churn. Goal: Implement model-specific predictive prefetch + soft-reservation memory profiles that reserve transient working-set slices based on a short-horizon forecast of active KV pages, reducing allocation churn and eviction thrashing while preserving batching efficiency. This ticket defines the design, microbenchmarks, integration plan, and rollout for the feature.
milestones: 2026-03-05: model telemetry sweep and per-variant occupancy histograms collected
2026-03-12: predictive prefactor model implemented and integrated into allocator hints
2026-03-25: staged rollout to canary fleet and perf dashboards verified
steps: Collect per-worker temporal occupancy histograms for Llama/Mistral/Qwen under representative traffic
Train a lightweight predictive heuristic (exponential smoothing + token-phase features) to estimate short-horizon hotset growth
Expose allocator hint API: reserve_fraction and prefetch_window per model-variant config
Implement soft-reservation: allocator sets aside contiguous slab segments marked preferential for KV residency; eviction penalized until reservation window expires
Add prefetcher: prewarm KV pages for forecasted keys on warmup events and after long pauses
Integrate with continuous batching: coordinate reservation size with batch size hints to avoid starving batches
Run microbenchmarks and automated longseq perf tests; iterate on thresholds
perf_targets: Reduce OOM occurrences in long-context synthetic workloads by >= 95% compared to baseline
Lower 99th percentile tail-token-latency by >= 20% for multi-stream long-dialogue tests
Keep steady-state token throughput within 3% of baseline for p95 batching mix
Memory overhead from reservations <= 6% of device RAM on average across variants
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests for allocator hint paths and prefetcher added and passing
Benchmarks show perf_targets met on internal canary cluster
No new class of tail regressions observed in CI 72-hour soak
Rollout playbook documented with rollback hooks and thresholds
Design doc and model-config schema reviewed and approved by Runtime and Infra leads
risks: Over-reservation could reduce effective capacity and increase cost for Dedicated customers
Prediction model misfires could prefetch cold pages and increase memory pressure
Interaction with third-party quantization kernels may alter page residency patterns
Edge-case workloads with adversarial token pacing might force oscillations in reservation behavior
